items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5227               REVISED 05/26/11

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to repeal certain provisions of the general municipal law relating to
urban renewal agencies; to repeal certain provisions
of the general municipal law
relating to industrial development agencies;
to repeal
certain provisions of the public authorities law relating
to certain authorities;
and to transfer any books, records and remaining rights of any
dissolved authority
to an identifiable location

PURPOSE:
This bill would repeal the statutory authorization for certain urban
renewal and industrial development agencies that have ceased
operations, have dissolved by operation of law or were never
established, and would vest their records, property, rights, titles
and interest, and all obligations and liabilities in the municipality
in whose interest such agencies were created.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
This bill would repeal the statutory authorization for the following
urban renewal and industrial development agencies:

Sloatsburg Urban Renewal Agency
Beacon Community Develop Agency

Ogdensburg Urban Renewal Agency
Long Beach Urban Renewal Agency
Village of Johnson Urban Renewal Agency
Village of Hilton Urban Renewal Agency


Oneonta Urban Renewal Agency
Village of Liberty Urban Renewal Agency

JUSTIFICATION:
This bill would repeal the statutory authorization for certain urban
renewal agencies and industrial development agencies which are either
defunct or which were never ultimately established by local law. The
agencies listed in this bill have been determined inactive by the New
York State Authorities Budget Office, Department of Economic
Development, Office of the State Comptroller, or Commission on Public
Authority Reform, based on consultation with the affected local
government.

Although these agencies no longer function, their authorization
continues in State Law. This bill would repeal the statutory
authorization for certain industrial development agencies which are
either defunct or which were never ultimately established.
The agencies listed within its provisions have been determined
inactive by the New York State Authorities Budget Office, Department
of Economic Development, Office of the State Comptroller, or
Commission on Public Authority Reform, based on consultation with the
affected local government, and none has any outstanding debt or other
obligations.

Accordingly, this bill would advance the State's effort to maintain an
accurate inventory of agencies, and abolish unnecessary sectors of
local government.

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
None Noted, as the dissolved entities never operated

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
This is a new bill.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This bill would take effect 60 days after it becomes a law.
